ranking.note: Explicit prerequisite for #10102 and #19460, so it cannot sit below them in review order.
Still the category-defining PR, but placed after its stated dependency #29409.
Moved up: it is a stated prerequisite for #10102 (and shares sync logic with wallet rescan), so it should not trail the interface features it enables.
Raised to P2 and moved up to match #36105: both are wrapper-level platform bugs that make multiprocess binaries unusable (here on Arch-style install layouts, issue #35785).
Lowered to P4: superseded by #35037 per the author's own draft note, so the FD-exhaustion problem is already covered elsewhere.
Lowered to P4: an internal mining-state refactor that leaves IPC protocols, serialization and process management untouched, so it has little claim on IPC review attention.

inconsistencies: Dependency chain: #29409 -> #10102 -> #19460 -> #19461. Review in that order; the later PRs contain only their final commit on top of the earlier branches.

#34978 and #35037 solve the same problem (file descriptors not reserved for IPC listeners/connections). #35037 is the agreed approach (per-address limits on -ipcbind) and should be reviewed first; #34978 was drafted in its favour and is effectively redundant.
#36190 is stacked on #36105 and only tests behaviour introduced there; #36105 must be reviewed first or #36190 is untestable on its own.

Windows work overlaps: #32387 is the foundational IPC/libmultiprocess Windows port, while #35887 (-ipcfd -> -ipcchild rename, follow-up to merged #35084), #36105 and #36190 are wrapper/arg follow-ups. Reviewing #32387 sets the constraints the smaller Windows PRs depend on.

#35932 and #36097 both carry temporary libmultiprocess subtree commits pending upstream (libmultiprocess#335 and #342); their Core-side changes can be reviewed now but land order is governed by the subtree sync.
#35581 sits in this category but is mining-category work by the category definition (no change to IPC mechanics); it is listed here mainly because it touches mining interface bindings.
result.notes: The band spread is intentional: three P1s (the Chain capnp wrapper, the multiprocess centerpiece, and the shutdown-race crash fix), a broad P2 tier covering platform coverage, DoS/FD safety, mining-interface completeness and the wallet/GUI separation milestones, then tests/build-hygiene at P3 and superseded or out-of-scope work at P4.
